newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FCC rejects Ameritech's long-distance bid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FCC rejects Ameritech's long-distance bid.

text.p: Regulators on Tuesday rejected Ameritech Corp's request to provide long-distance telephone service, thwarting the carrier's bid to be the first Baby Bell to offer such service since the 1984 breakup of the old AT&T.

But in a partial victory for Ameritech, the Federal Communications Commission provided a detailed road map for how the Chicago-based carrier and other regional Bells can enter the $80-billion long-distance business.

The FCC, in turning down Ameritech's request, said that the company had not yet fully opened its local phone business in Michigan to long-distance companies and others wanting to offer their own brand of local service.

But the agency said that the company had made progress. Ameritech had sought permission to offer long-distance dialing to Michigan residents, one of five Midwestern states in which the carrier provides local phone service.

Last year's telecommunications act gives the Bells the chance to offer long-distance calling to local customers. The carriers must first prove that they have opened their local phone monopolies to new competitors.
The Bells were barred from getting into the long-distance business after they were spun off from the old "Ma Bell" during the AT&T breakup.
